findings.reason: The protected solution is concise, conventional, and interview-ready. The low, high, maximum_distance, required, left, right, stations, and k names expose the answer bounds, feasibility candidate, station count, and original gaps directly, with no generic local named index.

For an original gap g and candidate maximum D, splitting the gap into segments of length at most D requires ceil(g / D) pieces and exactly one fewer new station; this also gives the correct one-fewer result when g is exactly divisible by D. Summing that requirement over independent gaps makes feasibility equivalent to required <= k, and stopping once the sum exceeds k cannot change an infeasible verdict. The predicate is monotone in D. Initially high is the largest original gap and is feasible without additions, while zero is below every positive feasible answer. Each midpoint update preserves the optimum between low and feasible high. Seventy halvings make the final feasible upper bound much closer than the accepted tolerance, and unused stations can be added without increasing its maximum gap.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 774, Python, and the native minmaxGasDist(stations, k) interface. Authenticated source evidence confirms 10 through 2000 strictly increasing integer positions from 0 through 100000000, exactly k from 1 through 1000000 new stations placed anywhere on the x-axis including non-integer positions, minimization of the largest adjacent distance, and acceptance within 1e-6 of the optimum. The app-local adapter preserves that contract.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2066071109 are algorithmically identical: both initialize the same zero-to-largest-gap search interval, perform 70 midpoint checks, sum ceil(gap / candidate) - 1 over adjacent stations with the same early exit, move the feasible upper or infeasible lower bound, and return the upper bound. Their only structural differences are the required Solution.minmaxGasDist wrapper and Python typing dialect.

The repaired three-tier workloads keep the source-legal minimum of 10 original stations, hold eight unit gaps fixed, and grow k from 16 to 256 with one principal gap of length k + 1. In the final independent run, the exact protected source passed all 11 visible correctness cases and all three performance tiers with relative growth exponent +0.00 and a 1.01x largest runtime ratio. An independently correct incremental maximum-heap control matched every output but failed only performance with relative growth exponent +0.64, above the allowed +0.15, distinguishing fixed-precision O(n) feasibility passes from O(k log n) station-by-station allocation.

The Approach accurately derives the ceil-based station requirement, exact-divisibility adjustment, monotone feasibility predicate, feasible-upper-bound binary-search invariant, sufficient precision, and harmless unused capacity. Its O(n log(R / epsilon)) time and O(1) auxiliary-space claims match the protected implementation and branch manifest.

The modular Reference now preserves the statement's four-paragraph logical progression, exact two-example sequence without invented explanations, four constraints, and single source-native hint. It states exactly k arbitrary real-valued x-axis placements, the adjacent-gap penalty, and the 1e-6 acceptance tolerance in independent, contract-precise prose.

A fresh authenticated Premium review verified exactly two unexplained examples in source order, four constraints, one binary-search hint, and no source images, tables, diagrams, notes, or follow-up. The modular files are hash-bound in source_fidelity.json to source content hash d68f8ef4ab4ea5c09ea0e94389a250ebcf17a2602b8428033b56cf7c6f682bde, and the direct fidelity validator returns verified with no errors.

coverage: The authenticated Premium statement contains exactly two examples. Their exact station arrays, k values, and outputs now appear first in source order; the invented two-station third sample was removed.

Every former non-source correctness case and all three former benchmarks used only two or three existing stations and therefore violated the source minimum stations.length of 10. They were replaced with source-legal inputs, every ordinary case is now a visible sample or trial, and all float validators use the source acceptance tolerance of 1e-6 rather than 1e-5.

Contract boundaries cover 10 and 2000 existing stations, station coordinates 0 and 100000000, strictly increasing order, k values 1 and 1000000, and non-integer optimal placements. The maximum-station case exposed a false generic trace-cap failure, so lc_774 now has the reviewed one-million-event terminating safety budget and a focused regression test.

Material behavior covers equal and unequal original gaps, tied maxima, too few additions to reduce every maximum, exact and fractional subdivision, allocation across multiple gaps, high-precision balanced allocation, an isolated dominant gap, and the fact that exactly k additions may leave the optimum unchanged.

Every authored expected value was recomputed with an independent exact-rational maximum-heap allocation oracle, not the protected parametric search. That oracle, the protected app source, and immutable native Solution agreed on all 14 authored correctness-plus-benchmark inputs, 6144 exhaustive legal gap configurations, and 5000 deterministic random legal inputs; the protected source also passed the complete real-test path.

The repaired 16-, 64-, and 256-station-addition workloads remain hidden and performance-only, span 16x, use 10 existing stations, and make the independently correct O(k log n) heap control fail only the scaling verdict.
